title: Operator signs in by receiving a one-shot magic link in their inbox
asA: operator with a registered email address and no memorised password
iWant: to submit my address to a sign-in form and receive a single URL that signs me in when I click it
soThat: no password exists anywhere for me to lose, reuse, or leak

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /login renders a form with a single email field and a submit control. No password field is present anywhere on the page.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response body contains an input with type='email' and name='email', and no input with type='password' or autocomplete='current-password'

acceptanceCriteria.description: POST /login accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded with an email field and returns a 200 response confirming that if the address is registered a link has been sent.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the operator submits the form with a valid email string
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 200 and the body confirms that a link will arrive if the address is registered, without confirming or denying that this address is registered

acceptanceCriteria.description: A submission for a registered address causes exactly one email to be dispatched via the configured adapter, carrying a URL that resolves to GET /login/verify on this deployment with the minted token as the sole query parameter.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a registered principal submits the form
acceptanceCriteria.then: the email-delivery-adapter.send call fires exactly once with a body containing a URL whose path is /login/verify and whose only query parameter carries the token

acceptanceCriteria.description: Following the emailed URL to GET /login/verify with a valid unconsumed unexpired token issues a session and redirects the operator to the configured post-sign-in landing route.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the operator follows the emailed URL within the token's validity window
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is a 302 to the configured post-sign-in route and carries a Set-Cookie header issuing a fresh session handle

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /login/verify with a missing, malformed, unknown, expired, or already-consumed token returns a 401 with a generic sign-in-failed response and no session issue.
acceptanceCriteria.given: GET /login/verify is called with any token value that does not resolve to a valid unconsumed unexpired record
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 401, no Set-Cookie is emitted, and the response body reveals nothing about which failure class the token fell into
